newsitem.title: USA: China resold Argentine soyoil, U.S. exporters say.
newsitem.headline: China resold Argentine soyoil, U.S. exporters say.

text.p: China has resold between 25,000 and 50,000 tonnes of Argentine soyoil to two trading houses in recent days, U.S. exporters said.
"It makes sense that they did it," said one senior soyoil trader. "After last week, the (CBOT) prices were just too high and they (China) had an opportunity to make some money."

Soy complex futures rose sharply after a bullish USDA report on U.S. soybean production and stocks on Friday. January soyoil closed at 24.65 cents a lb on Monday, up from 23.47 cents last Thursday before the USDA report.
"I know for sure it was done," said a second cash vegetable oil merchant, who estimated the size of the Chinese transaction to the two trading houses at 25,000 to 50,000 tonnes.
Talk of the Chinese deal helped pressure the CBOT board on Tuesday, floor sources said. At 1245 CST, January soyoil was down 0.23 cent per pound at 24.42 cents.
